subject: Difficulty passing input values as arguments to function after substitutions

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Difficulty passing input values as arguments to function after substitutions
parts:
Almost surely I've taken a completely wrong angle on this. 

The story is this: Given a function f(a, b), let the user select a or b as the "unknown" x and select a value for the other argument from a slider. For instance, return this f(input$a, "x") and plot f as a function of "x". 

My real-world function has several arguments and complicated expressions.

My problem is in "constructing" the function's reactive arguments. 

I defined a globalArgs vector in global.R

globalArgs <- c(a = "a", b = "b")

In server.R, I have the following:

    Args <- reactive({
        # 1. copy arguments stored in global.R
        v <- globalArgs
        # 2. replace selected parameter with "x"
        v <- gsubvec(input$X, "x", v)
        # 3. replace all non-selected parameters a with input$a (2 steps!)
        v <- gsubvec(names(globalArgs), lapply(names(globalArgs), function(x) {paste0("ZZZ",x)}), v)
        v <- gsubvec("ZZZ", paste0("input","$"), v)
        # 4. Miracle occurs: input$a as.numeric with "x" as.character or something
        # 5. return a list to use with do.call
        v <- as.list(v)
        return(v)
    })

The problem is that Args() returns "input$a" and "x" with unwanted double-quotes "" around them. There may be other problems too.

You can see from the complicated steps I went through that I'm missing something from the "big picture".

Help is appreciated. The code is below for perusal.

The function gsubvec is in global.R, if you're interested.

library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8297064")
https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8297064

messages.subject: Re: Difficulty passing input values as arguments to function after substitutions
parts: Input$x is stored as a character field.  You want to pass the object reference, in which case it is get(input$x)
